newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen up by 5,000-10,000T - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen up by 5,000-10,000T - trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks are expected to increase by between 5,000 and 10,000 tonnes later on Tuesday while aluminiums and zinc stocks may fall marginally, Singapore base metal traders said.
They estimated that aluminium and zinc inventories would each fall by between 1,000-2,000 tonnes.
On Monday, New York traders estimated that LME copper stocks would decline by between 6,000-8,000 tonnes and their London counterparts put the drop at 5,000-8,000 tonnes.
Singapore dealers said they expected a small rise in total base metal stocks in the LME warehouse here as Chinese metal exports continued to head towards the city state.
I do not expect a big jump in stocks as most Chinese supplies have already been delivered earlier," said one European trader.
On Friday, local dealers said 20,000 tonnes of Chinese zinc was moving towards Singapore lured by high international prices for the metal.
The volume of copper in the LME warehouse in Singapore on Friday rose by 500 tonnes to reach 39,150 tonnes, up from 38,650 tonnes in the previous report.
Three month LME copper was quoted around $2,240/$2,245 a tonne at 0630 GMT, marginally higher than London's close on Monday.
Traders said LME copper is stuck in a range, but might attack the $2,235 support level later on Tuesday when the stock figures are released.
Cash copper prices were quoted at around $2,535/$2,345 a tonne with the backwardation, the premium of spot over forward prices, pegged at $293.
